actions.texte:
ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Investigating Multiple Modalities in Federated Multi-Task Learning
PROPOSAL: We propose an experiment to explore whether our approach can be applied in multi-modal settings by training models on text and image data, leveraging pre-trained Transformers and Vision Transformers as the foundation models.
CONTROLS: Compare with a approaches that integrate multi-modal data in a server, and an off-the-shelf federated learning framework, that only shares information across models per modality.
COST: 1000 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: Our approach should show improved performance in text-image classification tasks, given the improvement in cross-modal understanding, but might encounter difficulties in managing memory, and computational efficiency; this could suggest the need for spatially distributed, computes-specialized setup.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Universality of Parameter-Sharing in Heterogeneous Federated Learning
PROPOSAL: We propose a theoretical result that studies the conditions under which parameter-sharing across models of different architectures leads to a hierarchical representation space, where a bottom-up process allows lower-level representations to build upon each other and achieve better generalization.
CONTROLS: Rigorously compare with previous knowledge-distillation-based approaches, considering when they converge or remain sparse and under-connected in higher layers of the hierarchy.
COST: 0 GPU-hours (Theory-only proposal)
PREDICTION: We expect to demonstrate that hierarchical representation spaces are closely related to many empirical knowledge-distillation successes; critical missing pieces of our understanding will become clear to us while waiting for convergence, however parameter computations may be uncomputable proofs, at a strict computational feasibility, pushing us towards collapsing them, or changes in the theoretical setting possibly dedicated resolution.

ACTION: REVISE 2
TITLE: Universality of Parameter-Sharing in Heterogeneous Federated Learning
PROPOSAL: We revise the theoretical proposal to focus on the proportion of shared parameters in a multi-task setting, and predict that when the number of tasks increases, the optimal proportion of shared parameters decreases, and when the models are of different sizes, larger models benefit more from sharing larger numbers of parameters.
CONTROLS: Compare with previous approaches considering when they converge in the optimal shared parameter regime, or stuck in inefficient honeypot subspaces.
COST: 0 GPU-hours (Theory-only proposal)
PREDICTION: We expect to demonstrate a fundamental shift in the optimal proportion of shared parameters with increasing number of tasks, showing the necessity of scaling shared parameter to effectively deal with task complexity and convenience in resource restriction of a model with inferior scale, and possible power off sub-network that would ameliorate our models performance as computational increases ramp up.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Knowledge Aggregation through Locally Learned Embeddings
PROPOSAL: We propose an experiment to investigate a novel approach to knowledge aggregation in heterogeneous federated multi-task learning, where each local model learns a task-specific embedding space that captures the commonalities among tasks, and shares this space with other models for knowledge aggregation.
CONTROLS: Compare with previous models that rely on pre-defined cluster labels or unsupervised embeddings, and an approach that aggregates knowledge through a task-agnostic latent space.
COST: 2000 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: Our approach should outperform previous models on task transfer performance, particularly in multi-task settings, due to the task-specific embeddings, while encountering potential difficulties in coordinating the shared space across models.

ACTION: REVISE 1
TITLE: Investigating Multiple Modalities in Federated Multi-Task Learning
PROPOSAL: We revise the experiment proposal to focus on a more specific multi-modal task, such as fine-grained sentiment analysis on text and images, and investigate whether our approach can learn a shared representation space that captures both textual and visual features, while also adapting to the specific tasks and modalities of each user.
CONTROLS: Compare with an approach that integrates multi-modal data in a server, and an off-the-shelf federated learning framework that only shares information across models per modality, while keeping realistic model architectures and experimenting with various aggregation strategies.
COST: 1200 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: Our approach should show improved performance on fine-grained sentiment analysis, capturing both textual and visual features, but might encounter difficulties in balancing the trade-offs between modalities, e.g., longer training times due to increased complexity.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Sequential Federated Learning with Contrastive Representation Shift
PROPOSAL: We propose a theoretical result that studies the conditions under which a sequential federated learning framework with contrastive representation shift can align representations across models, by analyzing the behavior of the contrastive loss function under varying levels of model heterogeneity and task diversity.
CONTROLS: Compare with previous models that require architectural congruity or component-wise knowledge distillation, and analyze the convergence properties of the contrastive loss function in the face of model drift and task shift.
COST: 0 GPU-hours (Theory-only proposal)
PREDICTION: We expect to demonstrate that sequential federated learning with contrastive representation shift can effectively align representations across models, even in the presence of model drift and task shift, and provide insights into the role of model heterogeneity and task diversity in shaping the convergence behavior of the contrastive loss function.

ACTION: REVISE 4
TITLE: Sequential Federated Learning with Contrastive Representation Shift
PROPOSAL: We revise the theoretical proposal to incorporate a more explicit mechanism for handling model drift and task shift in the sequential federated learning framework, by introducing abaugh regularization term that encourages the models to adapt to changes in their local data distributions and task objectives over time.
CONTROLS: Compare with previous models that address model drift and task shift through periodic re-weighting or forgetting mechanisms, and analyze the empirical convergence properties of the augmented framework in the presence of model drift and task shift.
COST: 0 GPU-hours (Theory-only proposal)
PREDICTION: We expect to demonstrate that the augmented framework can effectively handle model drift and task shift, and provide insights into the trade-offs between adaptation and forgetting in the presence of changing data distributions and task objectives.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Federated Learning with Graph-based Knowledge Diffusion
PROPOSAL: We propose an experiment to investigate a graph-based approach to knowledge diffusion in federated learning, where the knowledge graph is dynamically updated based on the local models' performances and is used to select and weight the models' updates during the knowledge aggregation process.
CONTROLS: Compare with previous approaches that rely on traditional knowledge aggregation methods, and analyze the impact of the graph structure on the knowledge diffusion process and the overall performance of the federated learning system.
COST: 1500 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: Our approach should show improved performance on task transfer and knowledge diffusion, by exploiting the graph structure to select and weight the models' updates effectively, but might encounter difficulties in managing the complexity of the knowledge graph and the dynamics of the graph structure over time.

ACTION: REVISE 2
TITLE: Universality of Parameter-Sharing in Heterogeneous Federated Learning
PROPOSAL: We revise the theoretical proposal to focus on the conditions under which parameter-sharing across models of different architectures leads to improved generalization, and investigate whether the universality of parameter-sharing holds for different types of models, such as neural networks and transformers.
CONTROLS: Compare with previous models that rely on weight transfer or knowledge distillation to achieve generalization, and analyze the empirical convergence properties of the parameter-sharing model in the presence of model heterogeneity.
COST: 1000 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: We expect to demonstrate that parameter-sharing can lead to improved generalization across models of different architectures, particularly in the presence of model heterogeneity, and provide insights into the role of regularizers and batch normalization in promoting robust generalization.

ACTION: REVISE 5
TITLE: Federated Learning with Graph-based Knowledge Diffusion
PROPOSAL: We revise the experiment proposal to incorporate a more sophisticated graph embedding method, such as Graph Attention Networks (GATs) or Graph Convolutional Networks (GCNs), to learn task-specific and task-agnostic representations that better capture the relationships among the models and their tasks.
CONTROLS: Compare with previous approaches that rely on traditional knowledge aggregation methods, and analyze the impact of the graph structure and the graph embedding method on the knowledge diffusion process and the overall performance of the federated learning system.
COST: 1800 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: Our approach should show improved performance on task transfer and knowledge diffusion, by effectively capturing the relationships among the models and their tasks, but might encounter difficulties in managing the complexity of the graph structure and the graph embedding method, particularly for large-scale networks.

actions.texte:
ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Investigating the Effectiveness of Meta-Learning for Noisy Label Correction
PROPOSAL: Train various meta-learning models (e.g., MAML, Reptile) on a set of pre-training tasks with noisy labels, and evaluate their ability to correct labels and adapt to unseen noisy distributions. For each pre-training task, use a noisy version of the CIFAR-10 or CIFAR-100 dataset, and compare the performance of the meta-learned models to a strong supervised baseline (e.g., ResNet-18 with data augmentation).
CONTROLS: Compare to a baseline model trained on clean labels, and ablating the meta-learning process to understand its effect on the model's ability to correct labels.
COST: 100 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: Meta-learned models will show better generalization to unseen noisy distributions, but may not be as effective at correcting labels in strongly noisy scenarios.

These meta-learning models are designed to learn how to adapt to new situations by leveraging prior experience. By training them on a variety of noisy label scenarios, we may be able to develop a model that is more robust to label noise and can adapt to new and unseen distributions. However, there is a risk that the model may overfit to the pre-training tasks and fail to generalize poorly to scenarios with strong label noise.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Uncertainty-Aware Label Correction through Ensembling
PROPOSAL: Develop an ensemble method that leverages the uncertainty estimates of multiple neural network models to correct noisy labels. For a given sample, calculate the disagreement among the models and use it as a confidence measure. Select the model with the highest confidence for label correction. Evaluate this method on several real-world datasets (e.g., WebVision, ImageCLEF) with varying levels of noise.
CONTROLS: Compare ensemble methods (e.g., bagging, boosting) to individual models, and ablate the uncertainty estimates to understand their impact on correction accuracy.
COST: 200 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: The uncertainty-aware ensemble method will outperform individual models, especially in scenarios with moderate to high label noise.

This ensemble approach leverages the strengths of multiple models to correct noisy labels. By selecting the most confident model for label correction, we can reduce the impact of label noise and improve the overall accuracy of the model. The uncertainty estimates serve as a quality indicator, signaling when multiple models disagree or have low confidence in their predictions. This method has the potential to perform well across various datasets and noise levels.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Adversarial Training for Robust Label Correction
PROPOSAL: Propose an adversarial training framework that simultaneous minimizes the prediction loss on clean labels and maximizes the loss on noisy labels. Train a discriminator to distinguish between clean and noisy labels, and an encoder-decoder architecture to correct noisy labels. Evaluate the robustness of this framework on various real-world datasets (e.g., ImageNet, Clothing1M) with instance-dependent noise.
CONTROLS: Compare the adversarial training framework to traditional supervised learning and other label correction methods, and ablate the effect of different discriminator architectures and learning rates.
COST: 300 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: The adversarial training framework will significantly improve the robustness of label correction, especially in scenarios with instance-dependent noise.

This approach tackles noisy labels from a different angle by incorporating an adversarial training step. The discriminator helps the encoder-decoder architecture identify the noisy labels, and the encoder-decoder corrects these labels while learning to focus on the clean labels. This method has the potential to robustly correct labels even when there is significant instance-dependent noise. However, there is a risk of overfitting to the discriminator or encoder-decoder architecture.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Transfer Learning for Noisy Label Correction with Weak Supervision
PROPOSAL: Investigate the use of transfer learning for noisy label correction by initializing a model on a weakly supervised dataset (e.g., annotation noise or incomplete annotations) and fine-tuning it on a target dataset with noisy labels. Evaluate the performance of this approach on several real-world datasets (e.g., WebVision, ImageNet) with varying levels of noise and task complexities.
CONTROLS: Compare the transfer learning approach to traditional supervised learning and other weakly supervised methods, and ablate the effect of different pre-training tasks and fine-tuning techniques.
COST: 150 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: Transfer learning with weak supervision will be beneficial for noisy label correction, especially when the pre-training dataset has similar task complexities or distributions as the target dataset.

This approach leverages the pre-training on weakly supervised data to provide a strong initialization for the noisy label correction task. By fine-tuning the pre-trained model on the target dataset, we can adapt to the specific noisy label distribution and task requirements. However, the choice of pre-training tasks and fine-tuning techniques may significantly impact the final performance.

ACTION: REVISE 3
TITLE: Adversarial Training for Robust Label Correction (Revised)
PROPOSAL: Refine the adversarial training framework (turn 3) to incorporate a self-supervised pre-training step, where the model learns to predict a hidden representation of the input data. This pre-training step helps the model to focus on learning meaningful representations, rather than just memorizing labels. Evaluate the effectiveness of this revised framework on several real-world datasets (e.g., ImageNet, Clothing1M) with instance-dependent noise.
CONTROLS: Compare the revised adversarial training framework to the original version, and ablate the effect of different pre-training tasks and adversarial training losses.
COST: 350 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: The revised adversarial training framework will significantly outperform the original version, especially in scenarios with instance-dependent noise, by learning more robust and meaningful representations.

This revised approach aims to improve the generalizability of the adversarial training framework by incorporating a self-supervised pre-training step. This allows the model to focus on learning more general and meaningful representations, rather than just memorizing the noisy labels. This should lead to better performance on instance-dependent noise, but the increased complexity may also increase the risk of overfitting.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Active Learning for Noisy Label Correction
PROPOSAL: Develop an active learning strategy for noisy label correction, where the model selects the most informative samples for human annotation or labeling correction. Evaluate this strategy on several real-world datasets (e.g., ImageNet, WebVision) with varying levels of noise and task complexities.
CONTROLS: Compare the active learning strategy to traditional passive learning and other sample selection methods, and ablate the effect of different selection criteria and annotation budget.
COST: 250 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: The active learning strategy will significantly improve the efficiency of noisy label correction by focusing on the most informative samples, but may not generalize as well to unseen scenarios due to the limited annotation budget.

This approach tackles noisy labels by actively selecting the most informative samples for correction, rather than relying on all samples. By doing so, we can reduce the annotation burden and improve the efficiency of noisy label correction. However, the effectiveness of this approach will depend on the selection criteria and annotation budget, and may not generalize well to new scenarios with different noise distributions or task complexities.

ACTION: ADD

PROPOSAL: Develop a self-supervised learning approach where the model is trained to predict its own noisy labels, and uses this prediction to correct its own labels. Evaluate this approach on several real-world datasets (e.g., ImageNet, Clothing1M) with instance-dependent noise.
CONTROLS: Compare the self-supervised learning approach to traditional supervised learning and other self-supervised methods, and ablate the effect of different training objectives and architectures.
COST: 400 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: The self-supervised learning approach will demonstrate promising results in correcting its own noisy labels, but may require careful tuning of the training objectives and architectures to avoid overfitting.

This approach has the potential to greatly simplify the noisy label correction process by allowing the model to correct its own labels. By training the model to predict its own noisy labels, we can leverage its internal representation to identify and correct the noisy labels. However, this approach may require careful tuning of the training objectives and architectures to avoid overfitting, and may not generalize as well to unseen scenarios or noisy label distributions.

COST: 300 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: The robust regularization technique will significantly improve the robustness of the model to noisy labels, but may increase the risk of overfitting to the noisy labels.

This approach aims to promote robustness to noisy labels by adding a regularization term to the loss function that encourages consistent predictions. By doing so, we can encourage the model to produce more accurate and robust predictions, even when the labels are noisy. However, this approach may increase the risk of overfitting to the noisy labels, if the regularization term is too strong.

By doing so, we can encourage the model to learn more general and robust representations that are less susceptible to label noise. However, this approach may increase the risk of overfitting to the tasks or requiring a large amount of additional data.

actions.texte:
ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Evaluation of Popular Methods for Class-Conditional Label Noise
PROPOSAL: Compare the effectiveness of popular class-conditional label noise filtering methods (e.g. Method1: symmetric Noise, Method2: Asymmetric Noise, Method3: Noise-Adaptive Loss), using the CIFAR-10-C dataset as a benchmark for class-conditional noise.
CONTROLS: Compare to a baseline where no noise filtering is applied.
COST: 20 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: The experiment will reveal that Asymmetric Noise outperforms the other methods, by providing a more nuanced understanding of the noise patterns in the CIFAR-10-C dataset. However, the results might fail to generalize to instance-dependent noise due to the discrepancy in noise modeling.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Investigating Instance-Dependent Label Noise
PROPOSAL: Develop a learning framework to model instance-dependent label noise using a meta-learning approach, incorporating a noise model learned from a validation set to correct the noisy labels. Evaluate this framework on the Clothing1M dataset, a benchmark for instance-dependent label noise.
CONTROLS: Compare to methods that do not incorporate a learned noise model, such as Random Noise and Stratified Sampling.
COST: 30 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: The experiment should show that the meta-learning approach provides better performance and generalizability compared to traditional methods under instance-dependent label noise, but may be computationally expensive and sensitive to the quality of the validation set.

ACTION: REVISE
TITLE: Investigating Instance-Dependent Label Noise
PROPOSAL: Develop a learning framework to model instance-dependent label noise using a meta-learning approach (from turn 2), and refine it by incorporating self-supervised learning techniques (e.g., CPC, AAE) to better explore the data manifold and reduce the impact of noisy labels.
CONTROLS: Compare to the previous method, as well as other self-supervised learning methods that do not incorporate a learned noise model.
COST: 40 GPU-hours (includes training a self-supervised model and fine-tuning it on the meta-learning task)
PREDICTION: The revised experiment should provide more robust performance and possess more effective noise mitigation properties, but might require optimized hyperparameters settings to prevent degeneration into self-supervised learning.

TITLE: Designing a New RGB-Event Fusion Model with Temporal Attention for High-Frame-Rate Semantic Prediction
PROPOSAL: Design a new RGB-event fusion model, dubbed TEASER (Temporal Event Attention-based SEgmentation and Reasoning), which incorporates temporal attention to selectively focus on the most relevant events and RGB features. TEASER will be implemented using a transformer encoder-decoder architecture, where the encoder combines RGB features with event data, and the decoder produces a dense semantic map using attention-based queries. TEASER will be trained and validated on the KITTI dataset and the Devil_dataset (with Ground Truth) accessory.

PREDICTION: We expect TEASER to outperform the state-of-the-art RGB-event fusion models and the baseline model, especially in areas with high dynamic scenes. actions.texte:
ACTION: ADD
TITLE: RGB-Event Fusion with Hierarchical Attention for High-Frame-Rate Semantic Segmentation
PROPOSAL: This experiment proposes a novel RGB-event fusion approach that combines the strengths of both modalities using a hierarchical attention mechanism. The model will first encode each modality separately using a 2D convolutional neural network (CNN) for RGB frames and a 1D CNN for event streams. A hierarchical attention mechanism will then selectively weigh the contributions of both modalities based on the spatial coherence and temporal relevance. The feature representations will be concatenated and passed through a series of sub-pixel convolutional layers to produce dense and detailed semantic segmentations.
CONTROLS: 
- Baseline 1: RGB-only semantic segmentation (e.g., FCN, U-Net)
- Baseline 2: Event-only semantic segmentation (e.g., strip-based methods)
- Ablation study: removing the hierarchical attention mechanism
COST: 120 GPU-hours ( training on a subset of the KITTI dataset and a few synthetic datasets)
PREDICTION: This approach should significantly outperform the RGB-only and event-only baselines, and maintain high accuracy across varying prediction intervals and dynamic scenes. However, performance may degrade in extreme scenarios with high object motion, occlusion, or sudden appearance/disappearance of objects.

ACTION: REVISISE
TITLE: REVISED: RGB-Event Fusion with Hierarchical Attention for High-Frame-Rate Semantic Segmentation
PROPOSAL: To improve the hierarchical attention mechanism, this revised experiment introduces a spatial attention module that selectively focuses on regions of interest in the RGB frame based on the event stream's relevance. Additionally, a dynamics constraints module will be added to reason about the temporal consistency of the event stream and ensure that the attention mechanism weighs the contributions of both modalities cohesively across time. The spatial attention module can be learned jointly with the hierarchical attention mechanism, allowing the network to adaptively select both temporally relevant and spatially coherent information.
CONTROLS: 
- Revised Baseline 1: RGB-only semantic segmentation (e.g., FCN, U-Net)
- Revised Baseline 2: Event-only semantic segmentation (e.g., strip-based methods)
- Ablation study: removing either the spatial attention module or the dynamics constraints module
- Comparison with the original hierarchical attention mechanism
COST: 180 GPU-hours (training on a larger dataset or with more iterations)
PREDICTION: This revised approach should provide even more robust performance, particularly in highly dynamic and fast-changing scenarios, where accurately capturing spatial context while inferring meaningful events becomes a great asset. It should minimize the "perceptual gaps" issue and produce more accurate segmentation across a wider variety of use cases.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Event-Initiated Temporal Propagation for Semantic Segmentation
PROPOSAL: In this experiment, we propose an event-initiated temporal propagation approach that complements the RGB-Event Fusion with Hierarchical Attention. The idea is to utilize the event stream as a guide for propagating semantic information across time, ensuring that predicted segments are temporally coherent and accurate even in the presence of discontiguous scenes or appearance/disappearance of objects. Specifically, we will introduce a graph neural network (GNN) module that takes as input the event stream and the predicted segmentations from the RGB-Event Fusion with Hierarchical Attention. The GNN module will iteratively refine the segmentations, promoting local consistency and ensuring that the predictions at any arbitrary timestamp are temporally spatially coherent.
CONTROLS: 
- Baseline 1: using the RGB-Event Fusion with Hierarchical Attention as the sole predictor
- Baseline 2: using a motion-compensated approach for propagating segmentations across time
- Ablation study: evaluating the importance of each component in the GNN module
COST: 180 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: This approach should bridge the gap between event-based perception and dense, high-fidelity semantic segmentation, substantially improving performance in dynamic and high-speed scenarios. Furthermore, the incorporation of the GNN module can mitigate issues with object occlusion, reappearing objects, and border movement.

ACTION: REVISE
TITLE: REVISE 2. Event-Initiated Temporal Propagation for Semantic Segmentation
PROPOSAL: To further improve the performance of the event-initiated temporal propagation approach, we will incorporate a memory module that retains past event information. This memory will enable the network to remember and utilize patterns and events that have occurred earlier in time, allowing for more accurate predictions even in the presence of short-term occlusions or temporary discontiguous scenes. The memory module can be implemented using a dynamically-updated graph or a recurrent neural network-based architecture, allowing the network to selectively retain and update relevant information.
CONTROLS: 
- Revised Baseline 1: event-initiated temporal propagation without memory
- Revised Baseline 2: RGB-Event Fusion with Hierarchical Attention as the sole predictor
- Ablation study: evaluating the impact of different memory architectures and retention strategies
- Comparison with the event-initiated temporal propagation baseline using a separate, predefined memory bank
COST: 200 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: This updated approach should demonstrate significantly improved robustness to partial occlusions, changes in scene dynamics, and short-term object disappearances, enabling the network to produce more accurate predictions across a broader range of scenarios and use cases.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Joint RGB-Event Attention and Scene Understanding Graph (JACESG) for High-Speed Scenes
PROPOSAL: This experiment introduces a novel approach, JACESG, that jointly models attention mechanisms for both RGB and event streams, and scene understanding as a graph-based reasoning. JACESG integrates RGB attention to focus on relevant regions of interest in the scene, event attention to capture temporally relevant events, and a graph neural network to reason about the spatial structure of the scene, enabling the network to produce dense and accurate semantic segmentations for high-speed scenes. JACESG can effectively capture object dynamics, occlusions, and scene changes.
CONTROLS: 
- Baseline 1: RGB-Event Fusion with Hierarchical Attention
- Baseline 2: Event-Initiated Temporal Propagation
- Ablation study: evaluating the impact of different integrated graphs and node features
COST: 300 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: This novel approach should provide state-of-the-art performance in capturing dynamic scenes, objects movement and rapid changes, using events information to facilitate decision on spatially-temporal interest. This could improve ability to choose most assets-light intra-dynamic-RGB execution of the every edge pixels in the haze.

TITLE: Scaled Scene Understanding through Perceptual Frames (SSF)
PROPOSAL: This experiment introduces a novel approach, SSF, that uses a hierarchical scene hierarchy to scale up the understanding of the scene, aligned with the high-speed dynamics of the events. SSF breaks down the scene into smaller perceptual frames, which are then processed and understood incrementally, allowing the network to handle high-speed scenes with minimal processing overhead. This hierarchical framework enables the network to preserve critical information, while effectively pruning away less relevant details, thus enhancing scalability.
CONTROLS: 
- Baseline 1: Event-Initiated Temporal Propagation (with additional processing overhead reduction attempts)
- Baseline 2: JACESG without hierarchical processing ( as downgrade mod etu nous Boynes CCnov CBD/i fotogr original.)  
- Ablation study: evaluating the impact of different perceptual frame hierarchies and processing strategies
COST: 250 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: This novel approach should enhance scalability by reducing processing overhead and preserving critical information, while maintaining accurate semantic segmentation. By aligning scene understanding with high-speed dynamics, SSF will aid real-world applications in autonomous driving, drone navigation, and quadruped robot navigation.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Semantic Embeddings for RGB-Event Fusion with Dynamic Normalization (SENDEDN)
PROPOSAL: This experiment introduces a novel dynamic normalization-based method for RGB-event fusion, SENDEDN, that enhances the fusion of RGB and event feature embeddings using a dynamic learnable normalization layer. SENDEDN adaptively normalizes the RGB feature embeddings based on the event features, preserving the information encoded in the event data and enabling more effective fusion. This adaptive approach allows SENDEDN to learn a more robust and real-time representation of the scene, leveraging the strengths of both RGB and event data.
CONTROLS: 
- Baseline 1: RGB-Event Fusion with Hierarchical Attention
- Baseline 2: JACESG without adaptive normalization
- Ablation study: evaluating the impact of different normalization strategies and SENDEDN's dynamic learnable normalization layer
COST: 220 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: This novel method should enhance the effectiveness of RGB-event fusion, preserving the information encoded in the event data, and enabling more accurate and robust semantic segmentation, especially in high-speed scenes with rapid changes.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Adaptive Attention Mechanism with Depth-Aware Graph for RGB-Event Fusion (AAGDE)
PROPOSAL: This experiment introduces an adaptive attention mechanism with depth-aware reasoning, AAGDE, that enhances RGB-event fusion by considering the depth information of the scene. AAGDE uses a depth-aware graph neural network to reason about the spatial structure of the scene, while an adaptive attention mechanism dynamically selects relevant features from both RGB and event streams based on the scene's depth. This approach enables AAGDE to better capture object depth, occlusions, and scene changes, leading to more accurate semantic segmentation.
CONTROLS: 
- Baseline 1: JACESG without depth-aware reasoning
- Baseline 2: SENDEDN without adaptive attention mechanism
- Ablation study: evaluating the impact of different depth-aware graph architectures and adaptive attention mechanisms
COST: 280 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: This novel approach should improve the accuracy of semantic segmentation by leveraging depth information to better capture object relationships and scene changes, resulting in more robust performance in high-speed scenes with occlusions and changes.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Uncertainty-Aware RGB-Event Fusion with Temporal Consistency (URTIC)
PROPOSAL: This experiment introduces an uncertainty-aware RGB-event fusion approach, URTIC, that incorporates temporal consistency constraints to ensure robustness against changing scene dynamics. URTIC uses a Bayesian neural network to estimate uncertainty in both RGB and event features, and then fuses the features with a temporal consistency loss function. This approach enables URTIC to adapt to changing scene conditions, avoid overfitting, and produce more reliable semantic segmentations.
CONTROLS: 
- Baseline 1: SENDEDN without uncertainty-aware reasoning
- Baseline 2: JACESG without temporal consistency constraints
- Ablation study: evaluating the impact of different uncertainty estimation methods and temporal consistency loss functions
COST: 320 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: This novel approach should significantly improve the robustness and reliability of semantic segmentation in high-speed scenes with changing dynamics, resulting in more accurate and stable performance compared to baseline methods.

PROPOSAL: This experiment conducts a comprehensive evaluation of the proposed RGB-event fusion methods (RGB-Event Fusion with Hierarchical Attention, Event-Initiated Temporal Propagation, JACESG, SSF, SENDEDN, AAGDE, and URTIC) on the KITTI, Cityscapes, and BDD100K datasets, which are challenging real-world benchmarks for high-speed semantic segmentation. The comparison will assess the methods' performance, robustness, and generalizability under varying scene conditions, object dynamics, and sensor noises.
CONTROLS: 
- Baseline 1: current state-of-the-art RGB-only and event-only methods
- Ablation study: evaluating the impact of each proposed method's components and variations
- Comparison of scene understanding and semantic segmentation performance
COST: 500 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: This comprehensive evaluation will provide a scientific foundation for high-speed semantic segmentation, highlighting strengths and weaknesses of each method and providing insights for future research and innovation in the field. The comparison will identify the most robust and generalizable approach(es) for real-world high-speed RGB-event fusion applications, such as autonomous driving, drone navigation, and robotics.

propositions.texte: This experiment proposes a novel RGB-event fusion approach that combines the strengths of both modalities using a hierarchical attention mechanism. The model will first encode each modality separately using a 2D convolutional neural network (CNN) for RGB frames and a 1D CNN for event streams. A hierarchical attention mechanism will then selectively weigh the contributions of both modalities based on the spatial coherence and temporal relevance. The feature representations will be concatenated and passed through a series of sub-pixel convolutional layers to produce dense and detailed semantic segmentations.

propositions.texte: In this experiment, we propose an event-initiated temporal propagation approach that complements the RGB-Event Fusion with Hierarchical Attention. The idea is to utilize the event stream as a guide for propagating semantic information across time, ensuring that predicted segments are temporally coherent and accurate even in the presence of discontiguous scenes or appearance/disappearance of objects. Specifically, we will introduce a graph neural network (GNN) module that takes as input the event stream and the predicted segmentations from the RGB-Event Fusion with Hierarchical Attention. The GNN module will iteratively refine the segmentations, promoting local consistency and ensuring that the predictions at any arbitrary timestamp are temporally spatially coherent.

PROPOSAL: REVISED 1: We propose an additional control for FEWN+ by introducing a strong event-only segmentation method with a temporal domain attention mechanism (TDM) as a baseline. PROPOSAL: Experiment: EDs-CINEMATIC - Event-Driven Streaming Characteristics Impact on Neuro-Ecological Modesto Active Technology. EDs-CINEMATIC will investigate the effect of event-stream characteristics, such as event density, variability, and spatial distribution, on the performance of FEWN+ and other baselines. This will provide insights into how event-stream quality affects high-frame-rate semantic perception.
CONTROLS: EDs-CINEMATIC will use synthetically generated event streams with controlled characteristics, as well as real-world data from various sources (e.g., EventCam, e-Oracam).
COST: Estimated 800 GPU-hours.
PREDICTION: The results will highlight the importance of considering event-stream characteristics when designing and optimizing event-driven high-frame-rate semantic perception systems.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Efficient FEWN+ Implementation on Edge Devices for Real-Time High-Frame-Rate Semantic Perception
PROPOSAL: Experiment: FEWN+ Edge-Q - Feasibility of Efficient FEWN+ Implementation on Edge Devices. FEWN+ Edge-Q will investigate the possibility of running FEWN+ on edge devices, such as NVIDIA Jetson series, using efficient hardware-accelerated APIs and low-latency optimization techniques. This will enable real-time high-frame-rate semantic perception on edge devices, which is crucial for applications like autonomous vehicles.
CONTROLS: FEWN+ Edge-Q will be compared to a CPU-only implementation of FEWN+, as well as other relevant edge-device-based models (e.g., MobileNetV2, ShuffleNetV2).
COST: Estimated 1200 GPU-hours (using a single high-end GPU for optimization and evaluation).
PREDICTION: FEWN+ Edge-Q will demonstrate that efficient FEWN+ implementation on edge devices is feasible, achieving real-time performance and high semantic segmentation accuracy.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Transfer Learning for FEWN+ on Limited-Training-Data Scenarios
PROPOSAL: Experiment: FEWN+ TLS - Transfer Learning for FEWN+ on Limited-Training-Data Scenarios. FEWN+ TLS will explore the use of transfer learning for FEWN+ in scenarios where limited training data are available. Pre-trained FEWN+ models will be fine-tuned on small-scale datasets, and their performance will be evaluated on a variety of tasks in autonomous driving, drone navigation, and quadruped robot navigation.
CONTROLS: FEWN+ TLS will be compared to traditional training (i.e., training from scratch on the small-scale dataset) and other transfer learning baselines (e.g., using a pre-trained backbone network).
COST: Estimated 1500 GPU-hours (using a single high-end GPU for fine-tuning and evaluation).
PREDICTION: FEWN+ TLS will show that transfer learning can significantly improve the performance of FEWN+ in limited-training-data scenarios, making it more practical for real-world applications.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Robustness Analysis of FEWN+ in Adverse Weather and Lighting Conditions
PROPOSAL: Experiment: FEWN+ RWA - Robustness of FEWN+ in Adverse Weather and Lighting Conditions. FEWN+ RWA will evaluate the robustness of FEWN+ in scenarios with adverse weather (rain, snow, fog) and lighting (night, low-light) conditions, which are common challenges in autonomous driving and robot navigation.
CONTROLS: FEWN+ RWA will use a variety of datasets with diverse weather and lighting conditions (e.g., FogBank, Cityscapes, KITTI) and compare FEWN+ to other state-of-the-art segmentation methods.
COST: Estimated 1000 GPU-hours (using a single high-end GPU for evaluation).
PREDICTION: FEWN+ RWA will demonstrate that FEWN+ is relatively robust to adverse weather and lighting conditions, showing improved performance compared to other segmentation methods, and highlighting areas for further improvement.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Conclusion and Future Directions for High-Frame-Rate Semantic Perception
PROPOSAL: This paper will provide a comprehensive conclusion of the FEWN+ framework, highlighting its strengths and limitations. The authors will also discuss future research directions for improving high-frame-rate semantic perception, including the integration of multiple event streams, the use of edge AI for real-time processing, and the development of more robust models for adverse weather and lighting conditions.
CONTROLS: Not applicable.
COST: N/A.
PREDICTION: The conclusion and future directions section will provide valuable insights and recommendations for the research community, laying the foundation for future advancements in high-frame-rate semantic perception.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Investigating a hybrid approach combining pre-textual 3D representation learning and per-scene optimization.
PROPOSAL: We propose to finetune a pre-trained 3D representation model (e.g. Pix2Vox 2.0) on a subject-specific dataset, and then use a per-scene optimization method (e.g. score distillation sampling) to refine the generated 3D asset for better identity preservation across viewpoints. We will also assess the impact of using different pre-textual objectives (e.g. reconstruction, depth estimation) on the final results.
CONTROLS: Baselines: no pre-training and no per-scene optimization; ablations: no pre-training, no per-scene optimization, and different pre-textual objectives; controls: comparison with state-of-the-art methods for subject-driven 3D generation.
COST: 1000 GPU-hours (finetuning a pre-trained model, ~100 hours; per-scene optimization, ~900 hours).
PREDICTION: This hybrid approach could achieve significant improvements over state-of-the-art methods for subject-driven 3D generation, especially when using pre-textual objectives that emphasize depth estimation or geometry preservation. However, the computational cost may be high due to the per-scene optimization step, which could limit its practical applicability.

PREDICTION: This approach could significantly improve identity preservation in subject-driven 3D generation by providing the model with explicit cues about the person's appearance and shape. However, it may also lead to overfitting if not carefully regularized, which could limit its applicability to real-world scenarios.

actions.texte:
ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Investigating the Role of Viewpoint-Aware Diffusion in Personalized 3D Generation
PROPOSAL: Train a variant of the bi-directional diffusion model (DALL-E variant) on 3D reconstruction benchmarks, specifically designed to predict the appearance of viewpoints that are not seen in the input, with a personalized token/slider adaptation similar to the 2D subject-driven generation. Use the "ONION" dataset for training and a custom dataset of personalized 3D scans for evaluation. Evaluate the model's ability to preserve the semantic identity of the subject across viewpoints and compare it to a baseline model that does not incorporate viewpoint-aware diffusion.
CONTROLS: The baseline model uses a standard bi-directional diffusion model without personalized token/slider adaptation. Ablation studies will also be conducted to evaluate the contribution of the personalized token/slider adaptation, viewpoint-aware diffusion, and the bi-directional architecture.
COST: Estimated 500 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: This approach will show improved performance in preserving semantic identity across viewpoints compared to the baseline, but may struggle to adapt to rare or novel viewpoints. Expected ACC and dice similarity gt/pt  +-/20%. It could fail if the viewpoint-aware diffusion component does not effectively capture the spatial coherence of the 3D generation task.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Investigating the Effect of Multi-View Consistency Loss on Personalized 4D Generation
PROPOSAL: Modify the Diffusion model used in experiment 1 to incorporate a multi-view consistency loss, similar to the "geometry or multi-view loss" term in multi-view 3D reconstruction. This loss will be calculated by predicting multiple viewpoints from the 4D output and enforcing consistency across these views. Use the "4D-ONION" dataset for training and evaluation, which contains animations of various subjects from multiple viewpoints. Evaluate the model's ability to preserve the semantic identity of the subject across viewpoints and motion.
CONTROLS: Comparisons will be made to experiment 1, which used a view-aware diffusion model without multi-view consistency loss. Additional ablation studies will be conducted to evaluate the contribution of the multi-view consistency loss and the 4D specific architecture of the diffsq sample distillation model used.
COST: Estimated 800 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: Incorporating multi-view consistency loss will improve generation quality and consistency across viewpoints and motion, but may introduce instability or overfitting. Expected improvements of 15-30% on quality metrics. It could fail if the model overfits to the multi-view consistency loss, or if the model is unable to generalize to out-of-distribution motion or viewpoints.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Evaluating the Impact of Image-to-3D Constraints on Personalized Generation
PROPOSAL: Train a masked autoencoder (MAE) architecture specifically designed for 3D reconstruction tasks, and fine-tune it on a dataset of aligned 2D/3D pairs. The MAE will be used as a pre-training step for the diffusion models used in experiments 1 and 2, to provide additional input constraints. Evaluate the effect of pre-training on the performance of the diffusion models in terms of quality and consistency of generated 3D/4D assets.
CONTROLS: A baseline diffusion model without pre-training will be compared to a model pre-trained using the MAE. Ablation studies will be conducted to evaluate the contribution of the pre-training step and the impact of using different pre-training datasets.
COST: Estimated 300 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: Pre-training with the MAE will improve the quality and consistency of generated assets, as it provides a general 3D prior that can aid in generating plausible novel views. Expected improvements of 10-20% on quality metrics. It could fail if the pre-training step overfits to the pre-training data or if the diffusion model is unable to adapt the pre-trained features to the personalized generation task.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Understanding the Effects of Domain Adaptation on Personalized 3D Generation
PROPOSAL: Adapt the view-aware diffusion model from experiment 1 to a new 3D generation task with a different object class (e.g., a different animal) using a domain adaptation approach. Use a dataset of 3D scans from the new object class to fine-tune the model and evaluate the extent to which the domain adaptation approach enables transfer learning across different object classes.
CONTROLS: Compare the results to a baseline model that is trained from scratch on the new dataset. Ablation studies will be conducted to evaluate the contribution of different domain adaptation methods on the overall performance.
COST: Estimated 600 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: The domain adaptation approach will improve the performance of the model on the new task, but the extent of the improvement will depend on the similarity between the source and target domains. Expected improvements of 20-40% on quality metrics. It could fail if the domain adaptation approach is not effective or if the model is not able to generalize to the new task.

CONTROLS: Compare the results to a baseline model that uses the multi-view consistency loss without the temporal component. Ablation studies will be conducted to evaluate the contribution of the temporal consistency loss on the overall performance.
COST: Estimated 700 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: The temporal consistency loss will improve the performance of the model on 4D generation tasks, but the extent of the improvement will depend on the complexity of the scene and the amount of temporal information available. Expected improvements of 15-30% on quality metrics. It could fail if the temporal consistency loss is too restrictive or if the model is not able to generalize to novel temporal patterns.

PROPOSAL: Train and evaluate the view-aware diffusion model from experiment 1 on a real-world dataset of 3D scans, rather than a synthetic dataset. Evaluate the effect of using real-world data on the quality and consistency of generated 3D outputs, and compare the results to a baseline model that uses synthetic data.
CONTROLS: Compare the results to the baseline model that uses synthetic data to generate 3D outputs. Ablation studies will be conducted to evaluate the contribution of real-world data on the overall performance.
COST: Estimated 900 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: The real-world data will improve the performance of the model on 3D generation tasks, but the extent of the improvement will depend on the quality and diversity of the real-world dataset. Expected improvements of 20-40% on quality metrics. It could fail if the real-world data is too noisy or biased, or if the model is not able to generalize to novel real-world scenarios.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Investigating the Role of Multi-Task Learning in Personalized 3D Generation
PROPOSAL: Train a multi-task model that learns to perform multiple tasks simultaneously, such as 3D geometry reconstruction, texture synthesis, and semantic segmentation, on a dataset of 3D scans. Evaluate the effect of multi-task learning on the quality and consistency of generated 3D outputs, and compare the results to a baseline model that performs a single task.
CONTROLS: Compare the results to a baseline model that performs a single task. Ablation studies will be conducted to evaluate the contribution of each task on the overall performance.
COST: Estimated 1000 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: Multi-task learning will improve the performance of the model on 3D generation tasks by learning complex relationships between tasks and leveraging shared features. Expected improvements of 25-50% on quality metrics. It could fail if the model is prone to overfitting or if the tasks are too unrelated.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Evaluating the Transferability of Personalized 3D Generation Models Across Datasets
PROPOSAL: Evaluate the transferability of personalized 3D generation models across different datasets, by fine-tuning a model trained on one dataset on another dataset. Evaluate the effect of transfer learning on the quality and consistency of generated 3D outputs, and compare the results to a baseline model that is trained from scratch on each dataset.
CONTROLS: Compare the results to a baseline model that is trained from scratch on each dataset. Ablation studies will be conducted to evaluate the contribution of transfer learning on the overall performance.
COST: Estimated 800 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: Transfer learning will improve the performance of the model on 3D generation tasks by leveraging the knowledge gained from the pre-training dataset, but the extent of the improvement will depend on the similarity between the pre-training and fine-tuning datasets. Expected improvements of 10-30% on quality metrics. It could fail if the models are not generalizable across datasets or if the fine-tuning dataset is too dissimilar from the pre-training dataset.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Investigating Informative Hand-Designed Representations for 3D/4D Personalization
PROPOSAL: We propose a hand-designed mixed-representation architecture for the input image/video and the generative model, which extracts informative features such as texture and shape cues from the input, and fuses them with high-level style representations learned from pre-trained style translation networks or text embeddings. We test this architecture on a custom dataset of synthetic 3D objects and videos of real-world objects, using metrics like FID and SSIM to evaluate the preservation of identity and fidelity to the input.
CONTROLS: We compare our mixed-representation architecture to several baselines: a vanilla 3D/4D generation model with random initialization, a state-of-the-art style translation network, and an image-to-image translation model finetuned on a small number of example images.
COST: 1000 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: We expect our proposed architecture to outperform the baselines in identity preservation and randomness, but might struggle with capturing fine-grained texture details due to the limited capacity of hand-designed representations.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Analyzing the Role of Early Fusion of Input and Generation Branches in Personalized 3D/4D Generation
PROPOSAL: We investigate whether early fusion of the input and generation branches can improve identity preservation andebevel the hallucination of unobserved viewpoints in personalized 3D/4D generation. We modify our mixed-representation architecture from Proposal 1 to fuse the input and generation features at the early stages of the model, and compare the results with the baseline architecture and a late fusion approach. We use the custom synthetic dataset and evaluate the results with metrics like RECALL and precision for viewpoint hallucination, as well as FID and SSIM for overall quality.
CONTROLS: We compare our early fusion approach to the baseline mixed-representation architecture, as well as a late fusion approach that combines features from both branches after several layers of processing.
COST: 300 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: We expect early fusion to improve viewpoint hallucination and identity preservation, but might struggle with over-specialization to the input view if the fusion occurs too early, resulting in decreased quality for other viewpoints.

ACTION: REVISE
TITLE: REVISED: Investigating the Robustness of 3D/4D Personalization to Input Variations
PROPOSAL: To improve the robustness of 3D/4D personalization to input variations, we modify the architecture to include a conditional refinement network that takes the input image/video and the predicted 3D/4D representation as input and outputs a refined representation that is more robust to pose, lighting, and other input variations. We evaluate the results using the custom synthetic dataset and metrics like robust FID and robust SSIM that capture the similarity between the generated representation and the target representation under input variations.
CONTROLS: We compare our revised architecture to the baseline mixed-representation architecture from Proposal 1 and evaluate the results under various input variations such as pose, lighting, and viewpoint changes.
COST: 1500 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: We expect the conditional refinement network to improve the robustness of 3D/4D personalization, but might struggle with balancing robustness and quality, potentially leading to over-fitting to the target representation.

ACTION: REVISE 2
TITLE: REVISED: Investigating the Role of Early Fusion of Input and Generation Branches in Personalized 3D/4D Generation
PROPOSAL: We study the effect of different fusion points for the input and generation branches, from an early fusion after the first convolutional layer to a late fusion after several layers of processing. We compare the results using the custom synthetic dataset and metrics like RECALL and precision for viewpoint hallucination, as well as FID and SSIM for overall quality.
CONTROLS: We compare our approach to the baseline mixed-representation architecture from Proposal 1 and evaluate the results under different fusion points and input conditions.
COST: 400 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: We expect early fusion to outperform late fusion for viewpoint hallucination, but might struggle with over-specialization to the input view if the fusion occurs too early, resulting in decreased quality for other viewpoints.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Investigating the Use of Unsupervised 3D Shape Reconstructions for Personalization
PROPOSAL: We propose an unsupervised 3D shape reconstruction approach as a pre-processing step to the 3D/4D generation pipeline, where we use a 3D reconstruction model to generate a rich 3D representation from the input image/video. This 3D representation serves as a powerful guide for the 3D/4D generation model, improving its ability to preserve the identity of the object and hallucinate missing viewpoints. We evaluate the results using the custom synthetic dataset and metrics like 3D IoU and FID for the reconstructed 3D representation, as well as RECALL and precision for viewpoint hallucination.
CONTROLS: We compare our approach to the baseline mixed-representation architecture from Proposal 1 and evaluate the results under different 3D reconstruction models and settings.
COST: 1200 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: We expect the unsupervised 3D shape reconstruction approach to improve viewpoint hallucination and identity preservation, but might struggle with capturing fine-grained details in the 3D representation, potentially leading to over-smoothing of the generated 3D/4D representation.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Evaluating the Importance of Capturing Viewpoint Cues in 3D/4D Personalization
PROPOSAL: We propose a novel viewpoint-centric loss function that encourages the 3D/4D generation model to capture viewpoint cues from the input image/video. This loss function is designed to measure the similarity between the predicted 3D/4D representation and the target representation under different viewpoints. We evaluate the results using the custom synthetic dataset and metrics like viewpoint-averaged FID and viewpoint-averaged SSIM, as well as visual inspections of the generated 3D/4D representations.
CONTROLS: We compare our approach to the baseline mixed-representation architecture from Proposal 1 and evaluate the results under different viewpoint sampling strategies and dataset sizes.
COST: 1000 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: We expect the viewpoint-centric loss function to improve viewpoint hallucination and identity preservation, but might struggle with balancing the importance of different viewpoints, potentially leading to over-focusing on a single viewpoint.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Assessing the Transferability of 3D/4D Personalization Models Across domains and Data Sizes
PROPOSAL: We investigate the transferability of 3D/4D personalization models across different domains (e.g., animals, vehicles, furniture) and data sizes (e.g., small, medium, large). We train and evaluate multiple models on different domains and data sizes and assess their performance using metrics like FID, SSIM, and viewpoint-averaged FID. We also analyze the robustness of the models to unseen domains and data sizes.
CONTROLS: We compare our results to a baseline approach of re-training the model on each new domain and data size.
COST: 600 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: We expect models to be more transferable across domains than data sizes, but might struggle with capturing idiosyncrasies of specific domains or data sizes, potentially leading to decreased performance.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Investigating the Impact of Adversarial Training on 3D/4D Personalization Models
PROPOSAL: We incorporate an adversarial training approach to improve the robustness of 3D/4D personalization models to input variations and potential attacks. We add a discriminator network to the model and use a loss function that encourages the generator to produce realistic and personalized 3D/4D representations while fooling the discriminator. We evaluate the results using metrics like robust FID and robust SSIM.
CONTROLS: We compare our approach to the baseline mixed-representation architecture from Proposal 1 and evaluate the results under different adversary strengths and data augmentations.
COST: 800 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: We expect adversarial training to improve the robustness of 3D/4D personalization models, but might struggle with balancing the trade-off between realism and robustness, potentially leading to over-smoothing of the generated 3D/4D representations.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Ablating the Role ofeach Component in 3D/4D Personalization Models
PROPOSAL: We conduct an ablation study on our 3D/4D personalization model to assess the importance of each component, such as hand-designed representations, early fusion, 3D shape reconstructions, viewpoint cues, transferability, and adversarial training. We evaluate the results using metrics like FID, SSIM, and viewpoint-averaged FID, and analyze the impact of removing each component on the overall performance.
CONTROLS: We compare our ablation results to the baseline mixed-representation architecture from Proposal 1.
COST: 400 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: We expect to identify the most important components that contribute to the overall performance of 3D/4D personalization models, but might struggle with isolating the individual effects of each component, potentially leading to over- or under-estimation of their importance.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Real-World Evaluation of 3D/4D Personalization Models on Public Datasets
PROPOSAL: We evaluate our 3D/4D personalization model on real-world public datasets, such as Behind-the-Scenes (BTS) and products from online 3D marketplaces. We use metrics like FID, SSIM, and viewpoint-averaged FID to compare our model's performance to state-of-the-art models and assess the generalizability of our findings to real-world applications.
CONTROLS: We compare our model to state-of-the-art 3D/4D generation models trained on real-world data, as well as to a baseline model trained on synthetic data.
COST: 2000 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: We expect our model to perform well on real-world datasets, but might struggle with capturing the complexity and variability of real-world data, potentially leading to decreased performance and requiring further refinement.

TITLE: Revisiting Baselines for Self-Speculative Decoding
PROPOSAL: Re-evaluate two recent self-speculative decoding methods, Lookahead decoding and Medusa, on a range of transformer architectures and datasets, focusing on their performance, efficiency, and stability on multi-turn conversation and machine translation tasks. 
CONTROLS: Compare these methods to standard speculative decoding and several established baselines: throughput-optimized decoding, sentence-parallel decoding, and prompt lookup decoding.
COST: 10 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: Lookahead decoding will demonstrate some speedup over standard speculative decoding, while Medusa will exceed Lookahead in efficiency for machine translation tasks, but might be outperformed by other baselines on conversation tasks; our analysis will highlight their strengths and weaknesses.

CONTROLS: Evaluate the task-aware self-speculative decoding method on a range of tasks, including machine translation, question answering, and summarization, and compare it to state-of-the-art self-speculative decoding methods.
COST: 18 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: The task-aware self-speculative decoding method will demonstrate improved performance and adaptability across different tasks, while maintaining competitive efficiency and effectivity compared to existing self-speculative decoding methods.

ACTION: ADD 6
TITLE: Automated Cascade Scheduler for Self-Speculative Decoding
PROPOSAL: Develop an automated scheduler that optimizes the cascade structure for self-speculative decoding, selecting the most effective combinations of draft models and tokens based on input sequences and computational resources.
CONTROLS: Evaluate the automated scheduler on a range of tasks and datasets, and compare its performance to human-designed cascades and state-of-the-art self-speculative decoding methods.
COST: 30 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: The automated scheduler will achieve near-optimal cascade structures and demonstrate significant speedups and accuracy improvements compared to manual approaches, while offering flexibility and adaptability to different input sequences and computational constraints.

ACTION: REVISE 6

actions.texte:
ACTION: ADD 1
TITLE: Investigating the feasibility of training-free self-speculative cascades
PROPOSAL: Implement and evaluate the three most promising on-the-fly self-speculative decoding methods - Lookahead decoding, SWIFT, and Fine-tuned early-stopped-inverse softmax (FESISM) - paired with retrieval-based prompt lookup decoding as the base drafter across a dataset of conversational dialogue from the MultiWOZ 2.1 benchmark.
CONTROLS: Compare with standard speculative decoding and with minimal retrieval-based drafting methods such as prompt lookup decoding alone; investigate the impact of varying the number of cascade rounds and the draft length at each level; compare the performance of the single-Best-Lookahead and multi-Best-Lookahead versions of Lookahead decoding in cascades.
COST: 1000 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: We expect to see speedups comparable to standard speculative decoding with a less-expensive retrieval-based drafter as the base model, but with the potential added benefit of adaptability and decreased memory usage in specific cases; however, variations of draft length and number of cascade rounds may significantly impact results.

ACTION: ADD 2
TITLE: Evaluating adaptations of self-speculative techniques for cascades
PROPOSAL: Extend the previous experiment to explore the performance of intermediate layers or blocks, efficient attention mechanisms, and lightweight draft heads for autoencoding hidden states, as alternatives to the on-the-fly self-speculative decoding methods used in proposal 1, across a range of downstream applications, including machine translation (WMT14 EN-DE) and summarization (CNN/Daily Mail).
CONTROLS: Control experiments should also compare the accelerations obtained with the different self-speculative techniques in cascades with those in non-cascade speculative decoding, as well as ablate the usefulness of intermediate cascade rounds in each variant.
COST: 1600 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: Cascade accelerations could potentially be improved using specific adaptation techniques, such as leveraging the shared weights of the target model and the draft model to boost acceleration or explored accelerated architectures that include both adaptations together as well, however we expect a potential widened performance gap for large transformer models due to trade-off challenges between size and current researcher- ability to reverse engineer deep models.

ACTION: ADD 3
TITLE: Assessing the adaptability of self-speculative cascades
PROPOSAL: Develop a set of adaptive strategies for choosing, during inference, which self-speculative acceleration technique and how many tokens to draft, taking into account the acceptance rate, cost, and variance of the different methods, with the goal of maximizing the overall walltime improvement of speculative decoding in real-world downstream applications.
CONTROLS: Investigate whether addition of an adaptive decision-making module that evaluates real-time model performance needs to individually handle all considered architectures, and evaluate its sensitivity to hyperparameter choices; test these adaptive cascades for comparison against the cascade that uses preselected of identified preliminary compound List of method constellations and throughout.
COST: 1800 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: Improved adaptivity should result in increased acceleration on a greater number of tasks, especially in aggregate assessment of practical areas such as multi-turn conversation or automatic question answering and this approach holds promise to effectively advanced match sets and rigorously discriminate critical pursuer candidates further based on risk assessments.

TITLE: Assessing the adaptability of self-speculative cascades
PROPOSAL: Modify the adaptive strategies developed in proposal 3 to also take into account the real-time characteristics of the input sequence and the target model, such as its length, sequence complexity, and availability of computing resources, with the goal of optimizing the walltime improvement of speculative decoding in real-world downstream applications; test the adaptive cascade using these modifications for improved adaptability to hardware and sequence length constraints.

ACTION: ADD 4
TITLE: Theoretical analysis of cascade speculative decoding
PROPOSAL: Develop a theoretical framework to study the performance of speculative decoding in cascades, focusing on the regime where multiple draft models are used in series; derive a set of sufficient conditions for the walltime improvement of cascade speculative decoding over standard speculative decoding, based on the acceptance rates and costs of the individual draft models.
CONTROLS: Examine the subtlety and robustness of the derived framework by comparing its predictions with the results of experiments on simulated and real-world datasets.
COST: Low, <1 GPU-hour
PREDICTION: The theoretical framework should provide a useful tool for understanding and optimizing the performance of cascade speculative decoding, even if the predictions may not always align perfectly with the actual experimental results due to the limitations of the assumptions made during the derivation of the framework.

ACTION: REVISE 4
TITLE: Theoretical analysis of cascade speculative decoding
PROPOSAL: Refine the theoretical framework developed in proposal 4 by incorporating the adaptive strategies for choosing the draft model and the number of tokens to draft, as well as the real-time characteristics of the input sequence and the target model; derive a set of sufficient conditions for the walltime improvement of adaptive cascade speculative decoding over standard speculative decoding.
CONTROLS: Apply the refined framework to the experimental results from proposals 1, 2, and 3 to investigate whether the framework can accurately predict the performance of adaptive cascade speculative decoding in real-world scenarios.
COST: Similar to 1 GPU-hour, as it is a refinement of the original proposal
PREDICTION: The refined framework should provide a more accurate and generalizable analysis of the performance of adaptive cascade speculative decoding, but may still require further refinement and validation to account for the complexities of real-world datasets and applications.

ACTION: ADD 5
TITLE: Experimental evaluation of cascade speculative decoding with multiple draft models
PROPOSAL: Conduct a large-scale experimental evaluation of the performance of cascade speculative decoding with multiple draft models, using a diverse range of downstream applications, including multi-turn conversation, machine translation, summarization, question answering, and mathematical reasoning; investigate the impact of various hyperparameters, such as the number of draft models, the sequence length, and the accuracy targets, on the performance of cascade speculative decoding.
CONTROLS: Compare the results with the state-of-the-art speculative decoding methods, as well as with the theoretical predictions from proposal 4; ablate the effectiveness of individual draft models and the cascade architecture.
COST: 4000 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: The experimental evaluation should provide a thorough understanding of the performance of cascade speculative decoding with multiple draft models, and the results will likely show that the cascade architecture can achieve significant speedups and improved efficiency in a variety of downstream applications.

ACTION: REVISE 5
TITLE: Experimental evaluation of cascade speculative decoding with multiple draft models
PROPOSAL: Refine the experimental evaluation developed in proposal 5 to focus on the adaptability of cascade speculative decoding to the characteristics of the input sequence and the target model, such as its length, sequence complexity, and availability of computing resources; investigate whether the adaptive strategies developed in proposal 3 can successfully adjust the performance of cascade speculative decoding in response to these characteristics.
CONTROLS: Compare the results with the state-of-the-art speculative decoding methods, as well as with the theoretical predictions from proposal 4; ablate the effectiveness of individual adaptive strategies and the interaction between them.
COST: Similar to 4000 GPU-hours, as it is a refinement of the original proposal
PREDICTION: The refined experimental evaluation should provide a better understanding of the adaptability of cascade speculative decoding and the effectiveness of the adaptive strategies developed in proposal 3, and the results will likely show that the adaptive cascade architecture can achieve improved performance and efficiency in a variety of downstream applications.

ACTION: ADD 6
TITLE: Towards real-world deployment of cascade speculative decoding
PROPOSAL: Develop a proof-of-concept implementation of cascade speculative decoding on a real-world large language model, such as T5 or a similar model, and deploy it on a cloud-based infrastructure or a computation cluster; evaluate the performance and efficiency of the implementation in a real-world scenario and investigate the feasibility of deploying cascade speculative decoding in a production environment.
CONTROLS: Measure the walltime improvement, memory usage, and accuracy of the implementation compared to standard speculative decoding; conduct a thorough system-level optimization of the implementation to minimize overheads and maximize efficiency.
COST: 6000 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: The proof-of-concept implementation should demonstrate the feasibility of deploying cascade speculative decoding in a real-world scenario, but will likely require further optimization and fine-tuning to achieve production-quality performance and efficiency.

ACTION: ADD 7
TITLE: Cascade speculative decoding for domain adaptation and meta-learning
PROPOSAL: Investigate the use of cascade speculative decoding for domain adaptation and meta-learning, where the goal is to adapt a large language model to a new domain or task with limited offline data; develop a framework for using cascade speculative decoding to accelerate the adaptation process and improve the performance of the adapted model.
CONTROLS: Compare the results with state-of-the-art domain adaptation and meta-learning methods, as well as with the cascade speculative decoding implementation developed in proposal 6; ablate the effectiveness of individual components of the framework.
COST: 5000 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: The framework should demonstrate the potential of cascade speculative decoding for domain adaptation and meta-learning, but will likely require further investigation and optimization to achieve state-of-the-art performance and efficiency.
